blocks.en:
“I don’t think I have ever done anything as peculiar in my life.
Among other things, it shows a young man looking with interest at a print
on the wall of an exhibition that features himself. How can this be?
Perhaps I am not far removed from Einstein’s curved universe.”
So wrote M. C. Escher about his 1956 lithograph Print Gallery .
Nearly half a century later, a mathematical analysis related its geometry
to an untwisted source image through a conformal power map z ↦ z α z\mapsto z^{\alpha} , α ∈ ℂ \alpha\in\mathbb{C} .
Building on this construction, we use a frozen text-to-image diffusion
model to generate new self-referential scenes.
Prompting alone does not enforce the recursion, while a post-hoc
transformation can leave structures poorly connected.
Applying the transformation during sampling is also insufficient:
the denoiser may “repair” the intended distortion or drift out
of the prescribed geometry.
We construct a generalized inverse T † T^{\dagger} of the non-invertible
image transformation T T , adapted to its recursive constraint.
In the idealized formulation, the Penrose identity T ​ T † ​ T = T TT^{\dagger}T=T makes T ​ T † TT^{\dagger} an idempotent projection onto geometrically
admissible images.
Yet denoising only the transformed image remains an out-of-distribution
task, even with projection.
We therefore braid denoising steps with T T and T † T^{\dagger} :
source-space steps develop the untwisted scene, while transformed-space
steps refine its appearance and connections in the final geometry.
We generate Print Gallery -like compositions and explore
further transformations.
Rather than distorting a finished image, we let the scene and its
distortion develop together. 1 1 1 The title echoes Hofstadter’s Gödel, Escher, Bach: an Eternal Golden Braid ( Hofstadter, 1979 ) .

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: “I went there expecting staircases coming out of the windows…” Roger Penrose, recalling his 1962 visit to M. C. Escher ( Wade, 2015 )
blocks.zh: "我在那里等待着楼梯从窗户出来..." 罗杰·彭罗斯(Roger Penrose),回顾1962年他访问M. C. Escher(Wade,2015年).

blocks.en:
Maurits Cornelis Escher was not trained as a mathematician. Yet his art both
inspired mathematicians and drew on their ideas. After encountering Escher’s
work, Roger Penrose began devising impossible objects. The triangle and
endless staircase he published with his father Lionel in 1958 subsequently
inspired Escher’s Waterfall and Ascending and Descending ( Penrose and Penrose, 1958 ; Kersten, 2018 ; Kersten, 2019 ) .
A different loop appears in the earlier Print Gallery (1956).
A young man studies a print of a town; following its buildings brings us
back to the gallery in which he stands. A picture contains the world that
contains it ( Museum Escher in The Palace, n.d. ) .

1958年他和父亲莱昂内尔出版的无尽楼梯
启发了艾舍的"瀑布与升降"(Penrose and Penrose,1958;Kersten,2018;Kersten,2019).
在更早的Print Gallery(1956)中出现了不同的环.
一个年轻人研究一个小镇的指纹, 沿着它的建筑给我们带来了
回到他所在的画廊 一张图片包含了世界
包含它("宫殿"中的"博物馆"(Museum Escher in The Palace, n.d.)).

blocks.en:
de Smit and Lenstra (2003) described the print’s idealized geometry through a
conformal power map connecting a scale-periodic source to its transformed
image. It specifies how coordinates correspond, not how buildings, objects, and
textures should connect. We seek to generate scenes composed within this
geometry, using a pretrained image model.

纹理应该连接。 我们试图产生场景 由这个
几何学,使用被预先训练的图像模型.

blocks.en:
Prompting for self-reference imposes no exact relation between image regions.
Applying the transformation after generation enforces repetition, but leaves
the model no opportunity to account for the resulting connections.
Introducing it during sampling lets the model respond to the geometry,
but subsequent denoising can alter corresponding regions independently or
“repair” the intended distortion. Here, distortion is not a defect to
remove, but part of the artistic intent.

blocks.en:
We use two coupled representations: an untwisted, scale-recursive source and
its transformed image. A reverse coordinate warp alone is insufficient:
the image transformation selects and repeats content, and
a denoised image need not remain in its range. We therefore construct a
matched generalized inverse T † T^{\dagger} that also acts on such images.
Here Penrose returns through generalized inversion ( Moore, 1920 ; Penrose, 1955 ) . In the continuous construction, T ​ T † ​ T = T TT^{\dagger}T=T ensures that an admissible transformed image survives a
round trip unchanged. Thus T ​ T † TT^{\dagger} is an idempotent projection onto
the range of T T , restoring the constraint after updates,
without a Euclidean nearest-point guarantee.

blocks.en: 1.1 Related work
blocks.zh: 1.1 相关工作

blocks.en: “Originality is merely an illusion.” — M. C. Escher ( Locher, 1982 )
blocks.zh: “原件只是一种幻想。” —— M. C. Escher (Locher, 1982).

blocks.en:
de Smit and Lenstra (2003) formalized the geometry of Print Gallery and
used it to reconstruct the missing central region. Cipolina-Kun et al. (2022) subsequently compared CoModGANs, LaMa, and GLIDE
for completing the artwork: they straightened it into several views,
inpainted these views, and transformed the completion back.
Generation in the straightened representation is a direct precedent. We generate new scenes and repeatedly update both
representations during sampling. Generative Escher Meshes ( Aigerman and Groueix, 2024 ) combines diffusion guidance
with geometric constraints to synthesize tileable shapes and textures.
blocks.zh:
斯密特和伦斯特拉(2003年)正式确定了印刷画廊的几何和
用来重建失踪的中部地区. Cipolina-Kun等人(2022年)随后比较了CoModGANs、LaMa和GLIDE。
他们为完成这部作品而修饰它,
将这些观点涂成漆,并将完成器转换回原样.
直截了当的代议制是一个直接的先例。 我们创造新的场景 并反复更新
取样时的说明。 基因 Escher Meshes(Aigerman and Groueix, 2024)结合了传播指导
并有几何限制来合成可平面形状和纹理.

blocks.en:
Iterated function systems and fractal image coding represent structure
through repeated contractive maps ( Hutchinson, 1981 ; Jacquin, 1992 ) .
Neural Collages ( Poli et al., 2022 ) learns contractive operators whose fixed
points represent images. Our geometry prescribes admissible images, with content from a frozen model.
Generative Powers of Ten ( Wang et al., 2024 ) coordinates diffusion
across scales for semantic zooms; ZoomLDM ( Yellapragada et al., 2025 ) learns generation at multiple magnifications. These methods allow content
to change with scale, whereas our construction repeats the same content. Fractal Generative Models ( Li et al., 2025 ) uses
architectural recursion without imposing this equality on outputs.

blocks.en:
DDRM ( Kawar et al., 2022 ) exploits the spectral structure of linear inverse
problems, while DDNM ( Wang et al., 2023 ) corrects clean-image estimates
using a generalized inverse. DPS ( Chung et al., 2023 ) uses approximate
likelihood guidance for noisy linear and nonlinear measurements. Π \Pi GDM ( Song et al., 2023 ) also uses pseudoinverse-based guidance,
including nonlinear and nondifferentiable measurement operators.
Universal Guidance, Self-Guidance, and fast constrained sampling provide
further ways to steer a frozen prior ( Bansal et al., 2023 ; Epstein et al., 2023 ; Graikos et al., 2025 ) .
Here the constraint relates regions of the generated image
to one another, and sampling alternates between source and transformed
representations using the matched operators.

blocks.en:
MultiDiffusion ( Bar-Tal et al., 2023 ) fuses diffusion paths under shared
constraints, and SyncTweedies ( Kim et al., 2024 ) synchronizes
clean-image estimates through a canonical representation.
Visual Anagrams ( Geng et al., 2024 ) combines denoising predictions
under orthogonal image transformations. LookingGlass ( Chang et al., 2025 ) extends this approach to latent flow models and
more general spatial warps through Laplacian-pyramid image processing.
Diffusion Illusions ( Burgert et al., 2024 ) optimizes images whose arrangements
reveal different interpretations. Tiled Diffusion ( Madar and Fried, 2025 ) enforces compatibility between tile boundaries, including self-tiling;
Refracting Reality ( Yin et al., 2026 ) synchronizes directly and
indirectly visible content using optical warps. These methods establish denoising across coupled views; our contribution
is a matched operator pair for scale-recursive geometry and its use in
sequential source/Escher sampling. The forward operator discards content
outside a selected source band, while the generalized inverse selects
its Droste extension. Their composition is an idempotent projector onto
the twisted image class, allowing the constraint to be restored without
compounding the warp. Braided sampling inserts source-space denoising
between the inverse and forward maps to develop the scene within this
recursive geometry.

Idempotent Generative Network ( Shocher et al., 2024 ) trains a generator
using an idempotence objective; here the geometric operator is specified
analytically and the image prior is frozen. Gofer and Gilboa (2024) develop generalized inverses for nonlinear operators,
including a norm-based pseudoinverse, while Ehrlich et al. (2026) construct surjective pseudo-invertible neural networks (SPNNs) and define
inversion through a bijective completion. These formulations distinguish algebraic consistency from
the criterion selecting an inverse.

blocks.en: 5 Limitations
blocks.zh: 5 限制

blocks.en:
The fixed recursion centre may miss the intended subject. In
Figure 9 (left), warm-up anchors the nest on a window
rather than the off-centre painter’s canvas. Optional time travel can
also amplify seams instead of smoothing them, as the waterfall example
shows (right pair). More generally, finite resolution and subsequent
denoising limit geometric consistency: the continuous identities do
not guarantee exact recursion in the final raster image.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
Braided sampling combines a frozen image model with matched geometric
maps to develop recursive scenes in source and transformed representations.
Despite finite resolution and imperfect scene consistency, the results
show how geometry can shape a composition throughout generation. “I never got a pass mark in math … mathematicians now use my prints to illustrate their books.” —M. C. Escher ( Ernst, 1976 )

显示几何在一代人中如何塑造一个构成。 数学家现在用我的指纹来说明他们的书。 M. C. Escher(恩斯特,1976年)
